intro: If you want a place in Uthai Thani town where you wake up, open the door and find a green garden with the Sakae Krang River right there — Sakaekrang Haven Homestay is a newly opened stay that's starting to get talked about among second-city travellers. It's a cluster of small chalets in a garden on the riverbank, freshly built and clean, with air-con rooms, private balconies and garden or river views, free parking, an Asian breakfast of local dishes and fruit, and a hands-on owner who looks after guests personally. Rooms start from around ฿1,200/night.

body.html: What sets Sakaekrang Haven Homestay apart from the usual places in Uthai Thani town is that it's a newly opened riverside homestay run hands-on by its owner. This isn't a multi-storey hotel but a few small chalets in a garden by the Sakae Krang River. Early reviews mention a friendly, attentive host, a peaceful atmosphere, and rooms that are new, clean and modern-looking. It suits travellers who value calm, cleanliness and being close to nature on the water over flashy facilities.

It sits within Uthai Thani town, on the bank of the Sakae Krang River in Sakae Krang sub-district — about 2 km from the town centre, a few minutes by car. The homestay is right on the water, looking out over the floating houseboats and riverside life that are so characteristic of Uthai Thani. Khao Sakae Krang, the hill with its sacred footprint pavilion and town views, is a short drive away. Wat Uposatharam, with its old mural paintings, and the Uthai Thani town market with the Trok Rong Ya old street are both a short drive too.

Rooms are air-conditioned chalets of about 24 sq.m. Each has a private balcony or terrace, a garden or river view, an en-suite bathroom with shower, a flat-screen TV, a desk and a kettle. There's a choice of King (one large bed) and Twin (two beds) rooms. Being a brand-new property, everything is fresh and well kept; early guests are complimentary about the cleanliness and the modern styling. Wi-Fi is free throughout, and there's a shared lounge and garden where you can sit and catch the river breeze.
"Small chalets in a riverside garden, a lovely and very helpful host, a peaceful setting, new clean rooms and a tasty breakfast — really enjoyed it."

Breakfast here is an Asian breakfast with local specialities and fruit, served homestay-style rather than at a big buffet — early reviews call it tasty and neatly presented. A draw for those driving is the free private parking, with bicycle parking too. Uthai Thani is a small, flat town, well suited to driving or cycling along the Sakae Krang River at dawn or dusk — the times the town looks its best. In the evening, sitting at the riverside lounge to watch the houseboats and the sunset is a scene you won't get at a typical in-town hotel.

To be straight with you, the main limitation comes from it being a small, newly opened homestay with only a few chalets. There aren't many reviews yet (it's new), and while the early scores are high, base your decision on the photos and details as well as the number. On long weekends and holidays the limited rooms book out fast, so reserve ahead. And because it's a homestay, there's no in-house restaurant or pool — meals other than breakfast mean a short drive into town, which isn't far. The riverside location also sits away from the busiest commercial strip, so it suits those who come to unwind quietly rather than step out straight into shops.

Overall, Sakaekrang Haven Homestay earns very high real-guest scores on booking platforms, even as a new property with a modest review count. It isn't a luxury hotel or a big resort, but measured on the cleanliness of brand-new rooms, the quiet Sakae Krang riverside setting, owner-led care, a tasty breakfast, free parking, and rates starting around ฿1,200 (rising with season) — it's a well-judged choice for sleeping by the water in Uthai Thani in a calm, warm way.

A tip drawn from the reviews: ask for a chalet facing the river if one's free, as the Sakae Krang river view is the standout here. Book ahead, especially over long weekends, since chalets are limited. Flag a late arrival time in advance, and walk or cycle along the river to the morning market for the fullest taste of Uthai Thani's riverside life.

faqTitle: FAQ — Sakaekrang Haven Homestay Uthai Thani

faq.q: Where is Sakaekrang Haven Homestay in Uthai Thani, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay is at 88/8, Sakae Krang sub-district, in Uthai Thani town on the bank of the Sakae Krang River. It's about 2 km from the town centre, a few minutes by car, and close to Khao Sakae Krang, Wat Uposatharam and the town market with Trok Rong Ya old street — handy for an easy-going visit to Uthai Thani.

faq.q: How much does Sakaekrang Haven Homestay cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from around ฿1,200/night for a garden-view twin room of about 24 sq.m. There are Twin, King and river-facing rooms; all are air-conditioned with a balcony and en-suite bathroom. Prices rise with the season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Sakaekrang Haven Homestay have parking?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking, plus bicycle parking, ideal if you're driving. Uthai Thani is a small, flat town, easy to explore by car or by cycling along the Sakae Krang River.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they clean?
faq.a: Air-con chalet rooms of about 24 sq.m., each with a private balcony or terrace, a garden or river view, an en-suite bathroom, flat-screen TV, desk and kettle. As a newly opened property, everything is fresh and clean, and early guests praise both the cleanliness and the modern styling.

faq.q: Does Sakaekrang Haven Homestay serve breakfast or have a restaurant?
faq.a: It serves an Asian breakfast with local specialities and fruit, homestay-style. However, there's no on-site restaurant for other meals, so lunch and dinner mean a short drive into town, which isn't far — there are plenty of eateries and markets in town to choose from.

faq.q: Who is Sakaekrang Haven Homestay best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for travellers who want to sleep by the Sakae Krang River in a calm, clean, warm way — couples, small families, or drivers who value the riverside setting and owner-led care. It isn't about luxury or resort-style facilities, but it's well-judged for a night or two on a comfortable budget.
